#### §21: Contexts

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-21.1 | §21.1 | HIST, ARB | `setjmp`/`longjmp` are assembly in the C layer (`machine/setjmp.S`). The `jmp_buf` layout is ABI (OD-1), with pointer mangling and CET shadow-stack unwinding. Library functions that are async-signal-safe keep no drop-carrying Rust state across interruptible points, so a `siglongjmp` out of a handler does not skip destructors (F37). |
| D-21.2 | §21.2 | HIST | **Internal:** a safe `Fiber` coroutine API over `rt::context` and `machine/context.S`. **Boundary:** `makecontext`'s variadic `int` arguments go through a C variadic adapter (F11). |
| D-21.3 | §21.1–21.2 | KERN | **Shadow stacks** (refines D-21.1). Linux enables a user shadow stack only when the C library asks for it (`arch_prctl(ARCH_SHSTK_ENABLE)`, Linux 6.6+); glibc 2.39 does so only on request (tunable). Liella never asks, so no shadow stack exists in a Liella process and `longjmp`/`setcontext` have nothing to unwind. The `jmp_buf` and `ucontext_t` keep their shadow-stack fields (ABI) and Liella writes 0 there. Enabling shadow stacks is future work with its own decision. (Amended by D-21.5, D-21.6.) |
| D-21.4 | §21.1 | HIST | **The `setjmp` symbol does not save the signal mask**, as the spec states (§21.1: "`setjmp` on glibc does not save the mask either"); it is `_setjmp`. **Divergence found (phase 6, for the owner):** the host glibc 2.39 binary disagrees: its `setjmp@@GLIBC_2.2.5` loads 1 into `%esi` before `__sigsetjmp` (the BSD behaviour; `objdump -d` of `libc.so.6`). C code never sees the difference, because `<setjmp.h>` defines `setjmp` as `_setjmp`; only a call through the symbol itself (an address taken, another language's binding) does. **Owner ruling (2026-10-01): confirmed.** Liella follows the spec; the difference from the host glibc is documented in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`. |
| D-21.5 | §21.1–21.2 | KERN | **Jumps, contexts and vfork keep a user shadow stack matching the stack** (SHSTK-OPT-IN, owner ruling #7728; amends D-21.3, whose "Liella never asks" still holds until SHSTK-ENABLE: nothing enables the shadow stack yet, and without one every path below is skipped by a zero test of `rdssp`, a no-op then). Interface: Intel SDM vol. 1 ch. 17 (`rdssp`, `incssp`, `rstorssp`, `saveprevssp`, restore tokens) and the kernel's shstk documentation (`map_shadow_stack` with `SHADOW_STACK_SET_TOKEN`); evidence: plan/reviews/SHSTK-SCOPE.md. (1) **setjmp/longjmp** (`csys/src/machine/setjmp.S`): sigsetjmp stores SSP (0 without a shadow stack) at `jmp_buf` byte 80, private to libniji: past the kernel's 8-byte mask at 72, and word 10 of the 104-byte `__pthread_unwind_buf_t`, which libniji does not use (`boundary/src/cancel.rs` uses words 9 and 11). longjmp pops (`incssp`, at most 255 per instruction) to that SSP + 8 when the target is above the current SSP; it already resumes by a jump. (2) **Contexts** (`context.S`): `__ssp[0]` (byte 936) is the SSP the context resumes with (getcontext and swapcontext write it, 0 without a shadow stack). Resuming checks for a restore token at `__ssp[0] - 8`: present (a stack swapcontext left, or a makecontext stack), it drops the caller's entry, switches (`rstorssp`) and leaves a token on the stack it left (`saveprevssp`), so the saved context's `__ssp[0]` has its token; absent, the context is on the current stack and is popped to, as longjmp does. Every resume jumps to RIP (no `push`/`ret`). (3) **makecontext** (`boundary/src/context.rs`): the context starts in `niji_machine_start_context`, which `call`s the function (in r12) so its `ret` has a shadow-stack entry, and reaches uc_link's setcontext and the thread exit by `call` as well; with a shadow stack it maps one of `uc_stack.ss_size` rounded up to a page (a call takes 8 bytes of each stack, so the shadow stack cannot fill first), recorded in `__ssp[0..2]` (top, base, length). Nothing unmaps it: the interface has no end of a context (open for SHSTK-ENABLE; options in SHSTK-SCOPE item E). If the kernel refuses, `__ssp[0]` is 0 and the context runs on its resumer's shadow stack. (4) **vfork** (`vfork.S`): the child shares the parent's shadow stack and its calls overwrite vfork's entry, so both returns drop it (`incssp 1`) and jump. Unchanged and sufficient (SHSTK-SCOPE, measured): signals (the kernel saves and restores SSP), thread start and exit, cancellation (its buffers are longjmp targets, item 1) and posix_spawn's `CLONE_VM\|CLONE_VFORK` child, which never returns into the parent's frames. Not handled: a jump or setcontext to a context captured on another shadow stack without a token (getcontext there; or a kernel-made signal `ucontext_t`, which has no `__ssp`): the target is popped to as if on the current stack, so the next `ret` faults rather than running on. Off-path cost: setjmp +3 instructions, longjmp, vfork and the context switch +4 each (register zeroed, `rdssp`, test, branch). Tests: `conformance/c/s21_shadow_stack.c` (clause s21_1_g_0; SKIPPED without user shadow stacks), `crates/core/tests/s21_contexts_clauses.rs`. (Amended by D-21.7.) |
| D-21.6 | §21.1–21.2 | KERN, COMPAT | **The user shadow stack is opt-in through the tunables, decided once at start-up from every start object's marking, and a later `dlopen` of an unmarked object is refused, kept or turns it off by mode** (SHSTK-ENABLE, SHSTK-SCOPE items B, C and K; owner ruling #7728, PROVISIONAL: opt-in as the reference, default-on decided later; amends D-21.3, whose "Liella never asks" now holds only while the tunables do not ask). Interface: the GNU C Library manual's hardware-capability tunables (`glibc.cpu.hwcaps`, `glibc.cpu.x86_shstk`), x86-64 psABI §2.1.7 (`GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_AND`, bit `SHSTK`, in a `PT_GNU_PROPERTY` note), the kernel's shstk documentation (`ARCH_SHSTK_ENABLE`, `ARCH_SHSTK_LOCK`, `ARCH_SHSTK_DISABLE`). Probe-settled against the reference on the N100 class (Intel CET, Linux 6.8). (1) **Tunables** (`niji::config`): `glibc.cpu.hwcaps=SHSTK` asks (exact spelling; `shstk` and `SHSTK_Usable` do not; within one hwcaps list the last of `SHSTK`/`-SHSTK` counts, and a later `glibc.cpu.hwcaps` entry replaces the whole list). `glibc.cpu.x86_shstk` (exact lower case; another spelling or value is the default; the last entry counts): `off` vetoes, `on` keeps the shadow stack on through an unmarked `dlopen`, `permissive` turns it off there instead of refusing. Not asked: nothing below runs (one test of a parsed byte). (2) **Start-up decision**: dynamic (`ld.so` link step), the AND of the marking of the program, every `DT_NEEDED` object, every preload, the interpreter and the C library; static (the Rust start), the one image's (its `PT_GNU_PROPERTY` through `AT_PHDR`). A start with any unmarked object stays off in every mode (`on` included, probe-settled). When all are marked, it is enabled from a frame that never returns (`niji_machine_shstk_enter`, `ld.so`'s own copy in `entry.S`): enable, then lock `shstk` and `wrss` (the reference's mask) unless the mode is `permissive`, which may have to turn it off later. A kernel or CPU without the feature refuses the enable and the program runs without. All of it is cold code reached only when asked. (3) **dlopen** (`niji_ld::shstk::on_dlopen`): with the shadow stack on, a marked object loads; an unmarked one is refused with a `dlerror` naming SHSTK (default), loads with the shadow stack kept (`on`), or loads after every thread's shadow stack is turned off (`permissive`: a broadcast as SHSTK-SCOPE item C prices it). (4) **One difference** (docs/differences-from-glibc.md): `glibc.cpu.x86_shstk=off` vetoes in static programs too, in either order with `hwcaps=SHSTK`, as the manual describes it; the reference's static start enables and locks there. No compatibility option: the difference arises only when one string both asks for and vetoes the shadow stack, and the reference's result is had by dropping `x86_shstk=off` (coordinator ruling #8101, provisional while the owner is asked: one rule everywhere, a user who says off gets off). Costs (N100 class, opt-in on vs off, libniji): start-up +160 (dynamic empty) to +1,180 (static) user instructions, +15k to +51k kernel instructions and +2 to +5 faults (the enable, lock and the shadow-stack mapping, and the cold code's pages); off (not asked): no measurable change. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/start_objects.rs` (linker-built marked and unmarked objects in every start position), `conformance/c/s21_shstk_optin.c` and `_static.c` (clause s21_1_g_0; re-exec per tunable row; SKIPPED without user shadow stacks). |
| D-21.7 | §21.2 | KERN, COMPAT | **With a shadow stack, contexts carry the raw SSP and a user-context mark, and setcontext resumes a kernel signal ucontext by popping to its interrupted SSP; makecontext unmaps a shadow stack when its stack memory is reused** (SHSTK-ENABLE; amends D-21.5 items 2 and 3, and its "Not handled" for signal contexts). Interface: Intel SDM vol. 1 ch. 17; the kernel's shstk documentation (a signal pushes the interrupted SSP with bit 63 set onto the shadow stack; `UC_SIGCONTEXT_SS` in the signal frame's `uc_flags`). (1) **Raw SSP**: getcontext and swapcontext store the SSP of their own call (`rdssp`, 0 without a shadow stack) in `__ssp[0]`; a resume adds 8. makecontext stores its token's address (top − 8). (2) **User-context mark**: with a shadow stack, getcontext, swapcontext and makecontext set `uc_flags` to 0. Without one they leave it as it was, as the reference does (probed: a 0xff..ff `uc_flags` survives all three), so default-mode programs see no change. (3) **Signal contexts**: setcontext, with a shadow stack and `UC_SIGCONTEXT_SS` (2) in `uc_flags` (the kernel sets it, with 1 and 4, in every signal frame), does not read `__ssp` (in the kernel's frame that byte is not the library's): it searches up from the current SSP for the first entry holding (its address + 8) with bit 63 set, the innermost signal frame's token (no return address or restore token has bit 63), and pops to that interrupted SSP, then resumes the registers as usual. Rule: such a setcontext resumes the innermost signal frame on the current shadow stack (the handler's own ucontext, the common use); a signal ucontext of an outer frame, or one saved and resumed after its handler returned, is not supported (the search finds the wrong or no token; no token: it runs off the shadow stack's top and faults). (4) **Difference**: with the shadow stack on, `uc_flags` of a user context reads 0 after getcontext, swapcontext and makecontext (docs/differences-from-glibc.md). No compatibility option: the mark is what lets setcontext tell the two kinds of context apart, `uc_flags` has no meaning for a user context, and leaving stale bits would make setcontext misread a user context as a signal frame. (5) **makecontext unmaps the shadow stack it made for the same stack memory before** (SHSTK-SCOPE item E; coordinator ruling #8100 on SHSTK-ENABLE's recommendation): the library keeps its own registry of the shadow stacks makecontext mapped, keyed by `uc_stack.ss_sp` (`boundary/src/context.rs`, module `registry`: an open-addressing table of key, base and length in anonymous memory, at most half full and doubled past that, under one lock that a `fork` child resets once the process has used it, D-18.8). When makecontext maps a shadow stack for a key it has seen, it records the new one and unmaps the earlier one: every context made on that stack memory before is over, since the new context's frames overwrite theirs. Only a mapping in the registry is ever unmapped, never `__ssp[1..2]` of a `ucontext_t` (a struct copy shares them; fresh memory holds garbage). Not unmapped (the residual): the shadow stack of stack memory that is freed and never given to makecontext again stays mapped until the process ends (the interface has no point where a context ends; freeing at thread exit would unmap stacks of contexts other threads still resume); one the calling thread is running on (makecontext on its own stack) is left mapped; a stack passed with a different `ss_sp` (an offset into the same memory) is a different key; a new key when the table cannot grow (no memory) goes unrecorded, as before this rule. Rule: resuming a context saved on a stack after makecontext was given that stack again is not supported (its shadow stack is gone: the next `ret` faults; without a shadow stack its frames were already overwritten). Cost, default mode (no shadow stack; Skylake-SP host, per call vs the merge base): getcontext and swapcontext the same as D-21.5's sequence (xor, rdssp, store, test, branch); the -2 instructions a mark written in every mode would save are not taken, so as not to change `uc_flags` there. Test: `conformance/c/s21_shadow_stack.c` step "setcontext from a handler to its ucontext" (5 frames inside the handler, the signal raised 10 frames down, then those frames return); on the N100 class it passes, and the same program linked with context.S without this branch exits by SIGSEGV. Item (5): the same program's step "makecontext on the same stack memory 64 more times" (the shadow-stack mappings in `/proc/self/smaps` keep their size), and the unit test `makecontext_shadow_stack_registry` in `boundary/src/context.rs` (the table: reuse returns the earlier shadow stack, half-full and doubling rules). |
